To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
annexins can be activated by various divalent metal ions other than calcium.

annexin-mediated vesicle aggregation can be driven by a wide range of metal ions, and the relative concentration ratios of metal ion in the immediate environment may be crucial to the functioning of annexin proteins.
the ability of metal ions other than calcium to induce annexin-induced aggregation of liposomes decreases in the order of Cd(II)>Ba(II), Sr(II) > Ca(II) >> Mn(II) > Ni(II) >> Co(II).
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanism of action of annexins, the effects of various metal ions on annexins and the potential role of annexins as targets for metal ion toxicity.
the role of divalent metal cations in the functioning of annexin proteins.
understanding the molecular mechanism of annexin-mediated aggregation and the role of metal ions in this process.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

annexins can bind to and induce aggregation of liposomes in the presence of a variety of metal ions, and that the ability of these ions to induce aggregation of liposomal membranes decreases in the order Cd2+ > Sr2+ > Ba 2+ > Ca 2+ >> Mn 2+ > Ni 2+ > Co 2+.
annexin-mediated liposome aggregation can be driven by different divalent metal cations.
annexin-mediated vesicle aggregation can be induced by any divalent metal ion that can induce the formation of a Ca2+-type annexin conformation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
annexin-mediated vesicle aggregation is a general phenomenon that may occur in the presence of different divalent cations.
annexins are Ca2+ sensors and that the binding of Ca2+ is not sufficient to trigger the conformational change that is necessary for annexin-mediated aggregation.
annexins can be used as a probe for studying the effects of metal ions on the membrane and protein interactions.
The main takeaway from our work is that
annexins are a family of proteins that can be activated by a number of metal ions other than calcium.
the aggregation of vesicles mediated by annexins is more sensitive to the presence of divalent metal cations than the binding of the proteins to the membranes of the vesicles.
annexin-induced aggregation of liposomes is not specific for Ca2+ and that annexin-mediated vesicle aggregation can be driven by a number of metal ions.
